title: Snag Mom Jeans vs. Lucy & Yak Addison: A UK fit guide for a smaller waist and wider hips
summary: Both jeans make room for hips without relying on conventional stretch denim, but they do it with different waist systems, leg shapes, length choices, and size labels. Here is how to choose when waist and hip measurements disagree.
author: Curvy& Editorial

sections.heading: Why this comparison is useful now
paragraphs: A recent UK-focused r/PlusSizeFashion question described wide hips and fuller thighs as the reason jeans shopping had become a task to postpone. Replies mentioned both Lucy & Yak and Snag, but the feedback was mixed: Lucy & Yak drew praise for material and pockets alongside a warning about sizing, while Snag received a concise recommendation for fit.

A second recent discussion from a shopper seeking UK 26–28 clothing described garments fitting the stomach but failing at the bust, length, shoulders, or sleeves. Together, the threads point to a broader lesson: the label is only the start. For jeans, waistband structure, hip ease, rise, fabric stretch, and leg length decide whether a brand works for a particular proportion.

sections.heading: The size labels use different languages
paragraphs: Snag's Mom Jean runs from A (UK 4) through J2 (UK 38), with a separate letter-number code for each listed UK size. The current chart assigns G2 to UK 26, H1 to UK 28, and H2 to UK 30. Those labels are internal to Snag; a familiar Snag tights size should not automatically be carried into denim without using the denim chart.

Lucy & Yak's Addison uses waistband labels such as W46 for UK 26 and W48 for UK 28. Its general body chart currently maps UK 26 to a 46.1-inch waist and 56.3-inch hip, and UK 28 to a 48.4-inch waist and 58.7-inch hip. The W number may look like a finished waistband measurement, but it functions as the product's size label. Always confirm whether a number describes a body, a nominal waist size, or the garment itself before comparing it with another brand.
bullets: Snag G2 = UK 26 on the current Mom Jean chart.
Snag H1 = UK 28 on the current Mom Jean chart.
Lucy & Yak W46 = UK 26 and W48 = UK 28 on the current Addison options.
None of those labels should replace the actual waist and hip ranges.

sections.heading: Snag uses a shaped mom-jean pattern with minimal stretch
paragraphs: Snag describes its Mom Jean as high-waisted, relaxed, tapered, and ankle length. The fabric is 99% organic cotton and 1% elastane, which the brand calls true non-stretch denim with only functional give. It offers short, regular, and long versions; the current product page lists garment inseams of 26.25, 28.125, and 31 inches.

The detailed size increments are useful for a pronounced waist-to-hip difference. Snag lists G2/UK 26 for a 115–120 cm waist and 141–146 cm hip, while H1/UK 28 covers a 121–126 cm waist and 147–154 cm hip. That is a charted body proportion, not a guarantee that the waistband will lie flat on every high hip or that the tapered leg will suit every thigh.

Because the denim has very little stretch, check the hip and upper-thigh path while sitting. A jean can close at the waist yet pull at the fly or form horizontal drag lines across the front hip. Those signs call for a different size or cut, not a judgment about the body.

sections.heading: Addison creates hip room with pleats and elasticated panels
paragraphs: Lucy & Yak describes the Addison as a high-waisted, full-length jean with a wide waistband, an elasticated back, elasticated side panels, and front pleats intended to fit loosely over the hips. The current mid-wash version is made from 100% organic cotton denim, so the adjustable room comes primarily from construction rather than elastane in the cloth.

That makes Addison a different silhouette from a classic tapered mom jean. The pleated front and looser hip are design features, so a shopper seeking a smooth, close front may interpret the intended volume as excess fabric. For a fuller hip and thigh with a smaller waist, however, the combination of structured denim and an elasticated waistband can reduce the need to size the entire leg up just to clear the hips.

The regular product page lists a 76 cm inside leg and offers petite, regular, and long options. Lucy & Yak's general guide says Tall changes length-related proportions without changing width, while its Petite line makes both length and some width-related adjustments and is limited to smaller sizes. Read the exact product's available fit options rather than assuming every size is made in every length.

sections.heading: When waist and hips point to different sizes, the pages need a second read
paragraphs: Snag's current Mom Jean product page says shoppers between sizes or split between waist and hip should choose the smaller size for the Mom Jean, while choosing the larger size for closer-fitting bootcut, kick-flare, or shorts. Its separate general denim guide currently says to prioritize the larger measurement because the denim has little stretch. Those instructions do not fully agree.

The safest editorial interpretation is not to choose one sentence on the shopper's behalf. Use the product-specific Mom Jean chart and calculator, then ask Snag to confirm the starting size if the waist and hip fall into different columns. Save the response with the order. A brand's support team can also clarify whether the recommendation reflects intentional ease in the current Mom pattern or a recently updated fit.

For Addison, compare both body measurements with the exact product chart and review the intended loose hip. If the waist is one size and the hip another, ask for the relaxed and gently stretched waistband plus the garment hip measurement. That is particularly important for resale, where previous washing and wear may have changed the elastic or denim.

sections.heading: Which jean is the better starting point?
paragraphs: Start with Snag Mom Jeans if you want a tapered ankle-length shape, very small size increments, and three defined leg lengths across a range that currently reaches UK 38. Start with Lucy & Yak Addison if you want a full-length, pleated shape with an elasticated back and side panels, and you prefer hip room created by the pattern rather than stretch fiber in the denim.

For a smaller waist and much wider hips, neither choice should be reduced to 'size for the hips' or 'size for the waist.' First decide whether you want the hip to look relaxed or relatively clean, then check whether the waistband can recover after sitting. If the waist gap is modest, alteration may preserve the right hip and thigh fit; if the rise, front pleats, or leg volume are wrong, a different cut is usually the better solution.
bullets: Measure waist, high hip, full hip, upper thigh, front rise, and inseam in centimetres and inches.
Compare the chart with a non-stretch jean you already like, not with leggings or stretch jeggings.
Check the fit seated before deciding; minimal-stretch denim needs enough room through the full hip path.
For secondhand Addison or Snag denim, request the label photo, flat waist, stretched waist, front rise, hip width, thigh, and inseam.
Confirm return or exchange terms before buying two sizes as an at-home fitting strategy.

researchNote: This article synthesizes two UK-focused public discussions from August and September 2026 and verifies size ranges, measurements, construction, fabric, and length information on the brands' official pages. Community recommendations are individual experiences. The noted conflict between Snag's product-specific and general denim sizing language was present on the public pages at research time.
